clue.text: House accommodating British man in America

indicators.note: accommodating means the house takes in a guest, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a house is a home

explanation.surface: A home puts up a visiting British man in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Hombre is Spanish-derived slang used in the American West for a guy or fellow.

clue.text: Millions read this novel

parts.note: it seems to describe a bestseller, but also hints at a famous Dickens title naming a widely read newspaper

explanation.surface: A bestselling novel has millions of readers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dickens novel's title contains the name of a British daily paper read by millions.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's 1854 novel set in industrial Coketown.

clue.text: Scrums in shopping centres, do you say?

indicators.note: do you say asks whether the word is spoken alike, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: malls are shopping centres

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether crowds jostling in shopping centres count as scrums.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a maul is a loose scrum-like tussle around the ball carrier.

clue.text: Singer's old LP reissued after Queen's comeback

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged record behind the queen piece
comeback means the queen abbreviation turns round

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher, Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: reissued means the record letters are put out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A singer's vintage album is re-released after the queen returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comeback' turns ER into RE; 'reissued' makes DPOLL from OLD LP.
explanation.definitionFit: A redpoll is a small finch, and songbirds are singers in crosswords.

clue.text: Form of courage shown by viscount in resort abroad

indicators.note: in places the viscount inside the rearranged letters
resort read as re-sort, to sort again, so the following word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman shows daring while on holiday at a foreign resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday place but is read as re-sort: BRAADO, the anagram of ABROAD, has V put 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a showy, boastful display of boldness, a swaggering kind of daring.

clue.text: Social security scrounger arranged brief stint out east

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A benefits cheat organised a short spell away in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A pejorative term for a migrant supposedly moving countries to claim welfare.

clue.text: South American writer, everyone concluded, lacks finish

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: lacks finish means the word drops its final letter

parts.note: ended means concluded

explanation.surface: Everyone agreed the Latin American novelist never quite finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabel Allende is a Chilean novelist, author of The House of the Spirits.

clue.text: Nation divided over independent film maker

indicators.note: divided means the word is split up and rearranged

parts.note: on can mean over, as in a talk on or over a subject

explanation.surface: A country is split over an independent director.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo Antonioni was an Italian director of L'Avventura and Blow-Up.

clue.text: Wild animal in former times seen round centre of Burundi

indicators.note: seen round means the old-times word encircles the middle letter

parts.note: once means formerly

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of Burundi

explanation.surface: A wild beast was once spotted in central Burundi.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard.

clue.text: Room At The Top frequently read in Latin translation?

indicators.note: read in places the frequently word after the Latin letter

parts.note: oft is a poetic word for frequently
a conversion is a translation from one form to another

explanation.surface: John Braine's novel Room at the Top is often studied in a Latin version.
explanation.walkthrough: Room at the Top is a 1957 novel by John Braine; the capitals hide a plain attic room.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic turned into living space is literally an extra room at the top of a house.

clue.text: Plump and a bit sad? Modify figure slightly

parts.note: plump can mean round, chubby
feeling down is being a little sad

explanation.surface: Someone stout and slightly gloomy is told to adjust a number.
explanation.definitionFit: To round down is to reduce a number to the nearest lower whole value, a small numerical adjustment.

clue.text: Reveal learner goes to public school

indicators.note: goes to says the school follows the learner

parts.note: L is the learner plate abbreviation
ETON is the famous English fee-paying public school near Windsor

explanation.surface: A learner driver heads off to a famous private school.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is an idiom for disclosing a secret.

clue.text: Try drink -a short, followed by beer

indicators.note: short means the drink is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: tea is a drink
stout is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Someone samples a drink and then has a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' docks TEA to TE; the '-a' printed beside drink restates that the A goes. Then 'followed by' adds STOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To test out something is to give it a trial.

clue.text: Intended to save note for fund

indicators.note: to save means the intended wraps round and keeps the note inside

parts.note: one's intended is one's fiance

explanation.surface: Someone engaged is told to put money aside for a fund.
explanation.definitionFit: To finance a project is to provide money for it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Feature of a Beatles album cover, appealing to wide range of tastes

definitions.text: Feature of a Beatles album cover
appealing to wide range of tastes

explanation.surface: A famous record sleeve image is described as having broad appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Abbey Road sleeve shows the four Beatles walking across a zebra crossing in the centre of the street.
explanation.definitionFit: The Abbey Road photo puts the band in the centre of the street; as an idiom, moderate and mainstream, avoiding extremes.

clue.text: Collection of tales about French prime minister

parts.note: de is French for of or about
David Cameron was UK prime minister 2010-16

explanation.surface: A book of stories concerns a French premier.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's fourteenth-century set of one hundred stories.

clue.text: Cleaner shows how to keep fellow at bay?

definitions.text: how to keep fellow at bay?

explanation.surface: A cleaning product reveals how to repel a man.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as DETER GENT, the word reads as an instruction to put off a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleaning agent; split, it suggests putting off a gentleman.

clue.text: Musician is so inclined to worry about volume

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters surround the volume
to worry something is to agitate it, so the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An anxious person fusses over how loud the sound is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worry' rearranges IS SO INCLINED TO into SECONDIOLINIST, and 'about' puts that round V.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestral player in the lower violin section is a type of musician.

clue.text: Jack and I keep cool in city abroad

indicators.note: keep in the sense of hold or retain, so the jack word holds the cool word within it

parts.note: in cribbage, his nob is the jack of the turned-up suit
to air something is to cool or ventilate it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Jack and the speaker stay calm in a foreign city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His nob' is the cribbage jack; NOB 'keep's AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya.

clue.text: Think what Orient rival might say

explanation.surface: Consider what a competitor of a famous Orient might remark.
explanation.walkthrough: A rival of the Orient Express, a train, might announce itself as 'I'm a (en)gine'.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine is to conceive or suppose; as the cryptic sense, a locomotive's clipped self-introduction.

clue.text: Wearing warm garment, one is sweating more?

indicators.note: the garment is worn round the one, so it contains it

parts.note: a jumper is a warm knitted garment
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone in a woolly sweater is perspiring more.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous people sweat, so more jittery is cheekily defined as perspiring more.

clue.text: Magistrate accepts rule, avoiding first drink

indicators.note: accepts means the magistrate takes in the other piece

parts.note: JP is a Justice of the Peace

indicators.note: avoiding first means the word loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: A magistrate abides by the rules, steering clear of the first drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A julep is a sweet drink, often a mint julep with bourbon.

clue.text: Daughter won't go in open-top car, being chicken?

indicators.note: won't go in says the daughter is left out of the car

parts.note: a roadster is an open two-seater car

explanation.surface: A daughter refuses to ride in a convertible, being cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: A roaster is a bird suitable for roasting, typically a fowl.

clue.text: Group of hospitals given support, it's announced

indicators.note: it's announced means the word is heard spoken, giving a homophone

parts.note: trussed means supported, held with a truss

explanation.surface: Hospitals receive extra backing, according to an announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain's NHS, a trust is the body running a group of hospitals.

clue.text: Piece of popular gospel music that's slow

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a well-loved hymn is played slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the Italian tempo marking for a very slow, broad movement.

clue.text: Sit-in organised by pupil briefly in school?

indicators.note: organised means the protest letters are arranged afresh
briefly means the pupil word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a tutee is a pupil

explanation.surface: Students stage a protest sit-in at school.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that an institute is only loosely a school; 'organised' and 'briefly' work on the protest word and the pupil word.
explanation.definitionFit: An institute is an educational establishment, hence the question mark for a loose sense of school.

clue.text: Writer is retiring on .. this?

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is reads in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An author stops work and lives off a regular income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' turns IS into SI; the whole clue also describes the income an author retires on.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension is the regular payment someone lives off after leaving work.

clue.text: Group determined to clinch record contract finally

indicators.note: to clinch means to grip, so the outer word holds the other pieces

parts.note: set can mean determined, resolved
an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of contract

explanation.surface: A band is keen to sign a recording deal at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A septet is a group of seven performers.
